quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space when passing. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly can make them lose control.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with rules about stereo volume.
A television show.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on all sides, in the back, and in the front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers about railroad crossings. It tells you a railroad crossing is ahead. Look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light.
A flashing red light.
A solid yellow light.
A solid red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car that honks first.
The car traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control, always let the vehicle coming from your right go first.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either side. Do not cross these lines except to turn left or pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing tracks and follow all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars, pedestrians, and bicyclists.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting expressways, when behind motorcycles or bicycles, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
questions.explanation: Move to the right when another driver passes you. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely and return to the right lane easily.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio so you can listen for a train.
Only go when a flagger tells you it is safe, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always slow down at railroad crossings. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: Which of the following increases a driver's crash risk?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone or any audio device can take your attention away from driving and increase your risk of a crash.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to make sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to make sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and check behind your car before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby. Look for pedestrians and obstacles.

questions.question: What should you do if a traffic light is not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your car off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers your intentions.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop and proceed carefully when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn cars that you are entering.
Stick part of your car onto the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and other traffic go first.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for a highway exit.
The maximum safe speed for a highway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for a highway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum safe speed for a highway exit. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: What will help someone recover from drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person recover from the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to use:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when stopped by a police officer?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel. Ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When can you proceed through a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic
After coming to a complete stop and confirming it is safe
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing down to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and confirming it is safe
questions.explanation: Always come to a complete stop at a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Proceed only when you are sure it is safe.
